#4. Target Construction
```{r}

create_targets <- function(df) {
  df <- df %>%
    arrange(sasdate)
  for (h in c(3, 6, 12)) {
    future_recession <- sapply(
      seq_len(nrow(df)),
      function(i) {
        future_rows <- (i + 1):(i + h)
        # Exclude observations without complete future data
        if (max(future_rows) > nrow(df)) {
          return(NA_integer_)
        }
        future_values <- df$USREC[future_rows]
        # Handle missing recession indicators
        if (any(is.na(future_values))) {
          return(NA_integer_)
        }

        # 1 if any future month is recessionary
        as.integer(any(future_values == 1))
      }
    )
    df[[paste0("Y_", h)]] <- future_recession
  }
  return(df)
}


macro <- create_targets(macro)
macro_fin <- create_targets(macro_fin)

#logic check
macro %>%
  select(sasdate, USREC, Y_3, Y_6, Y_12) %>%
  filter(
    sasdate >= as.Date("2007-01-01"),
    sasdate <= as.Date("2008-06-01")
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

```{r}
# forward fill if missig predictor values exist

forward_fill <- function(df) {
  predictor_cols <- setdiff(
    names(df),
    c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")
  )
  df %>%
    arrange(sasdate) %>%
    fill(all_of(predictor_cols), .direction = "down")
}

# modelling datasets
```

#7. LASSO model 
reusable function - have to think about the announcement delays from NBER, as mentioned by prof, this assumption may introduce lookahead bias... can consider incorporating announcement delays into model specification (18 months following Davig and Hall),, so like restruct training observations to those at least h + 18 months before forecast origin
```{r}
fit_lasso <- function(train_data, horizon, post=FALSE) {
  target <- paste0("Y_", horizon)
  # exclude variables that should not be predictors
  predictor_cols <- setdiff(
    names(train_data),
    c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")
  )
  
  # prepare x and y
  x_train <- as.matrix(train_data[,predictor_cols])
  y_train <- train_data[[target]]
  
  # estimate model
  model <- rlassologit(x=x_train, y=y_train, post=post)
  return(model)
}


forecast_lasso <- function(df, horizon, post=FALSE, test_start = as.Date("1986-01-01")) {
  target <- paste0("Y_", horizon)
  
  # exclude non-predictor columns
  predictor_cols <- setdiff(
    names(df),
    c("sasdate", "USREC", "Y_3", "Y_6", "Y_12", "sample")
  )
  df <- df %>% arrange(sasdate)
  
  # test observations with known outcomes
  test_indices <- which(
    df$sasdate >= test_start & !is.na(df[[target]])
  )
  results <- vector("list", length(test_indices))
  
  for (j in seq_along(test_indices)) {
    i <- test_indices[j]
    # latest training observation with completed target window
    train_end_idx <- i-horizon-1
    if (train_end_idx < 1) next
    
    # expanding training window
    train_data <- df[seq_len(train_end_idx),,drop=FALSE] %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[target]]))
    
    # check training sample
    if (
      nrow(train_data) < 50 ||
      length(unique(train_data[[target]])) < 2) next
    
    # fit model
    model <- fit_lasso(
      train_data = train_data,
      horizon = horizon,
      post = post
    )
    
    # predict using current month's indicators
    x_test <- as.matrix(
      df[c(i,i), predictor_cols, drop = FALSE]
    )
    probs <- as.numeric(predict(model, newdata = x_test, type = "response"))
    stopifnot(length(probs) == 2)
    prob <- probs[1]
    results[[j]] <- data.frame(
      sasdate = df$sasdate[i],
      horizon=horizon,
      post=post,
      actual = df[[target]][i],
      predicted_prob = prob
    )
  }
  bind_rows(results)
}

```

#8. Out of Sample forecasting

```{r}
datasets <- list(Macro = macro_model, Macro_Financial = macro_fin_model)
horizons <- c(3,6,12)
post_options <- c(FALSE,TRUE)

# store predictions
run_lasso_models <- function(datasets) {
  all_forecasts <- list()

for (dataset_name in names(datasets)) {
  for (h in horizons) {
    for (post_option in post_options) {
     model_name <- ifelse(post_option, "Post-LASSO", "LASSO")
     cat("Running:", dataset_name, h, model_name, "\n")
     result <- forecast_lasso(
       df = datasets[[dataset_name]],
       horizon = h,
       post = post_option
     )
     result$dataset <- dataset_name
     result$model <- model_name
     key <- paste(dataset_name, h, model_name, sep = "_")
     all_forecasts[[key]] <- result
    }
  }
}
  bind_rows(all_forecasts)
}

forecast_results <- run_lasso_models(datasets)

```

## POINT TO NOTE (TO ADD IN REPORT) Across all LASSO specifications and forecast horizons, the models produce an extremely confident false positive in April 2020. This may reflect the exceptional nature of the COVID-19 recession, which lasted only two months. Historically, severe deteriorations in macroeconomic conditions are associated with more persistent recessions, potentially leading the models to overestimate future recession risk. Furthermore, because the target variable captures recession occurrence strictly after the forecast-origin month, April 2020 is classified as a non-recession outcome despite being a recessionary month itself. This illustrates the sensitivity of recession forecasting to both unusual economic shocks and the definition of the forecasting target.

# 9. Evaluation of results

```{r}
evaluate_forecasts <- function(df, threshold = 0.5) {
  actual <- df$actual
  prob <- df$predicted_prob
  
  # convert probabilities into binary predictions
  predicted <- as.integer(prob >= threshold)
  
  # confusion matrix components
  TP <- sum(predicted == 1 & actual == 1)
  TN <- sum(predicted == 0 & actual == 0)
  FP <- sum(predicted == 1 & actual == 0)
  FN <- sum(predicted == 0 & actual == 1)
  
  # classification metrics
  precision <- ifelse(TP+FP==0,0, TP/(TP+FP))
  recall <- ifelse(TP+FN==0, NA_real_, TP/(TP+FN))
  specificity <- ifelse(TN+FP==0, NA_real_, TN/(TN+FP))
  f1 <- ifelse(precision+recall==0,0,2*precision*recall/(precision+recall))
  balanced_accuracy <- (recall+specificity)/2
  
  # probability based evaluation
  brier <- mean((actual-prob)^2)
  
  #ROC-AUC
  auc_value <- as.numeric(auc(roc(actual,prob,quiet=TRUE)))
  data.frame(AUC = auc_value, F1 = f1, Balanced_Accuracy = balanced_accuracy, Brier = brier)
}
```

```{r}
evaluation_results <- forecast_results %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~evaluate_forecasts(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()

print(evaluation_results, n=Inf)
```

Comparison between Macroeconomic indicators model and Financial + Macroeconomic variables model

```{r}
financial_comparison <- evaluation_results %>%
  select(dataset, horizon, model, AUC, F1,

    names_from = dataset,

  ) %>%

    AUC_gain = AUC_Macro_Financial - AUC_Macro,
    F1_gain = F1_Macro_Financial - F1_Macro,
    Balanced_Accuracy_gain =
      Balanced_Accuracy_Macro_Financial -
```

# 10.  Statistical significance of AUC improvements through block bootstrap (adapted from random forest analysis)

```{r}
block_bootstrap_auc_gain <- function(actual, prob_macro, prob_fin, block_length = 24, n_boot = 1000) {
  n <- length(actual)
  n_blocks <- ceiling(n / block_length)
  calculate_auc <- function(y,p) {
    if (length(unique(y))<2) return(NA_real_)
    as.numeric(auc(roc(
      y,p,
      levels=c(0,1),
      direction = "<",
      quiet=TRUE
    )))
  }
  # observed improvement of auc
  observed_gain <- calculate_auc(actual, prob_fin) - calculate_auc(actual, prob_macro)
  
  # bootstrap resampling
  gains <- replicate(n_boot, {
    starts <- sample(
      seq_len(n-block_length+1),
      n_blocks,
      replace=TRUE
    )
    idx <- unlist(lapply(starts, function(s){
      s:(s+block_length-1)
    }))[seq_len(n)]
    y <- actual[idx]
    calculate_auc(y, prob_fin[idx])-
      calculate_auc(y, prob_macro[idx])
  })
  gains <- gains[is.finite(gains)]
  if (length(gains)<100){
    stop("Too few valid bootstrap samples.")
  }
  data.frame(
    AUC_gain = observed_gain,
    CI_lower = unname(quantile(gains,0.025)),
    CI_upper = unname(quantile(gains, 0.975)),
    valid_resamples = length(gains)
  )
}

# pair predictions from both sets
paired_forecasts <- forecast_results %>%
  select(sasdate, horizon, model, dataset, actual, predicted_prob) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = dataset, values_from = c(actual,predicted_prob)) %>%
  arrange(horizon,model,sasdate)

# verify that outcomes match between the information sets
stopifnot(all(paired_forecasts$actual_Macro == paired_forecasts$actual_Macro_Financial))

# run bootstrap for each horizon and model
set.seed(1213)

lasso_auc_ci <- paired_forecasts %>%
  group_by(horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~block_bootstrap_auc_gain(
    actual = .x$actual_Macro,
    prob_macro = .x$predicted_prob_Macro,
    prob_fin = .x$predicted_prob_Macro_Financial
  )) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(significant = CI_lower > 0 | CI_upper < 0) %>%
  arrange(model, horizon)

print(lasso_auc_ci, n=Inf)
```
## Extension: LASSO with Selected Lagged Predictors according to Economic Intuition

1. Define lag specifications and add lag predictors

```{r}
lag_spec <- list(UNRATE = c(3,6),
                 PAYEMS = c(3,6),
                 CPIAUCSL = c(3,6),
                 HOUST = c(3,6),
                 S_P_500 = c(3,6),
                 T10YFFM = c(6,12))

data.frame(variable = names(lag_spec), available = names(lag_spec) %in% names(macro_fin_model))

# adding lag predictors to dataset
add_selected_lags <- function(df, lag_spec) {
  df <- df %>% arrange(sasdate)
  for(variable in names(lag_spec)) {
    if (!variable %in% names(df)) {
      next
    }
    for (k in lag_spec[[variable]]) {
      new_col <- paste0(variable, "_lag", k)
      df[[new_col]] <- lag(df[[variable]], k)
    }
  }
  return(df)
}

macro_lagged <- add_selected_lags(macro_model, lag_spec)
macro_fin_lagged <- add_selected_lags(macro_fin_model, lag_spec)
```

6. Comparison change in model performance of lagged predictors addition to the model

```{r}

# Match original and lagged forecasts by date and model
paired_lag <- forecast_results %>%
  select(sasdate, horizon, model, dataset,
         actual, prob_original = predicted_prob) %>%
  inner_join(
    forecast_results_lagged %>%
      select(sasdate, horizon, model, dataset,
             actual, prob_lagged = predicted_prob),
    by = c("sasdate", "horizon", "model", "dataset", "actual")
  )

# Compare performance on identical forecast dates
lag_performance <- paired_lag %>%
  group_by(dataset, horizon, model) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    original <- evaluate_forecasts(data.frame(
      actual = .x$actual,
      predicted_prob = .x$prob_original
    ))

    lagged <- evaluate_forecasts(data.frame(
      actual = .x$actual,
      predicted_prob = .x$prob_lagged
    ))

    data.frame(
      AUC_original = original$AUC,
      AUC_lagged = lagged$AUC,
      AUC_change = lagged$AUC - original$AUC,
      Brier_original = original$Brier,
      Brier_lagged = lagged$Brier,
      Brier_improvement = original$Brier - lagged$Brier
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

print(lag_performance, n = Inf)

```
